pages.text: $(l)Lamps$()$(br)The light bulb, circular lamp, light panel and aluminum lamp all work the same way. Place one on a face of an electric block: it takes power through its $(item)back$().

$(li)$(item)400 ohm$() consumer.$(li)Light level = $(item)voltage / 10$(), full brightness (15) from $(item)150 V$().$(li)A $(item)redstone signal$() switches it off.$(li)$(item)Burns above 1 A$(), so above $(item)400 V$().$(br2)$(l)Neon tube$()$(br)Neon tubes connect to each other like pipes and carry power along the line.

$(li)$(item)200 ohm$() consumer, light level = voltage / 10.$(li)$(item)Burns above 1 A$(), so above $(item)200 V$(). This is the lowest limit of all electric blocks: give neon its own low voltage network, through a transformer or a potentiometer.
Right-click any lamp or neon tube with a $(item)dye$() to change its color. Black and grays are refused.$(br2)A lamp burning out drops nothing, like every overloaded block.
